text: A selection is answered per case: the caller sends one POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer per selected case and assembles a TransferSelection element with an ordered results array (caseId, the assignment or the refusal messageId) and the done and total counts, in the caller's order, with the summary derived from the array and no second call.
why: The legacy screen sends one request per case and the legacy criterion fixes the outcome and the summary text but no source types the element, so the contract has to fix one shape or every consumer guesses.
read: Legacy story RWB E2 012 v2 sections 4, 13 and 16; FSD P3 A2.40.4.3 AC-EXC-P3-040-04; TSD P3 API-P3-006
impact: Fixes the screen model and the test rows; no set-level operation is added and the per-case operation stays unchanged, so a later set-level call would be a new version.

text: A refusal answers one element with the message ID, a reason code, the owner list with an open-case count and a cap each, or the current and target state, and the cap and the hold are read inside the operation before the first write, so a refused move changes nothing.
why: The criterion fixes what the user must see and no source types the answer; the cap and hold are columns of two tables and a read inside the operation is the only way to refuse before a write without a second call.
read: Legacy story RWB E2 012 v2 sections 4, 12 and 14; FSD P3 A2.40.3.1; TSD P3 T3.1
applied_in: Story sections 4, 5 (X3, X4, X6), 7 (AC5, AC7, AC12), 11, 12.1
confirm: Solution architect, P3 and the service owner of rwb-case
impact: The field names of the refusal shape the screen and the contract tests; a later rename is a contract change for the composite route.

text: The centre of excellence owns the values of LOV-TRANSFER-REASON and a change is a dated reference load approved by a second person; the six codes R01 to R06 are the intended set of DL23 and no client closes the set.
why: The screen must show the codes in force and the operation must refuse a code outside them, while no source names who may add or retire a code, so the change rule has to be assumed before the list can be treated as governed data.
read: Legacy story RWB E2 012 v2 section 3 and 13; TSD P3 LOV table; FSD P3 A2.40.3.1
confirm: Centre of excellence and the data steward
impact: The six codes stay data, so a new code is a reference load and not a release; a wrong owner would put a policy change behind a deployment.

text: The two activities of the manual path carry a provisional start-to-close of 10 s and schedule-to-close of 60 s, and the operator thresholds are provisional: a budget-breach share of 1 per cent of calls, a refusal rate per message ID, an at-cap rate per queue and a dead-letter depth of 1, each confirmed with the service owner before UAT.
why: The deployment must carry a value for each of them and no source gives one; the retry policy and the 2 s user budget are the only fixed numbers.
read: Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 14; TSD P3 T7 NFR-008; Architecture v5 slides 41 to 44
applied_in: Story section 12.5 of APP and CON; sections 11, 13 and 14 of OPS
confirm: Service owner of rwb-case and the DevOps lead
impact: Decides when an operator is paged and when a move is abandoned by the activity; a value that is too tight pages on a normal day, one that is too loose hides an outage.
